data.description:
# A committed lock turns any future advisory on a transitive dep into a build-stopping CI failure

## Why this exists

Closing `e47e-a33d-b9cf-4421` surfaced a `caused_by` edge to `ce5d-d352-9511-47bc` ("go uv-canonical
with a committed lock"), and the edge is accurate. It is NOT a defect in ce5d — committing a lock is
the right call for reproducibility — but it has a consequence nobody has a standing answer for:

**Before the committed lock, each install floated and a fixed upstream version was picked up silently.
Now a transitive dependency is frozen, so the moment an advisory is published against the pinned
version, the GATING `pip-audit` job fails on every change in flight, with no code change and nothing
the authors of those changes did wrong.**

That is exactly what happened with `click 8.2.1` / PYSEC-2026-2132: six changes from five different
work streams all went red simultaneously, and each author independently began diagnosing it.

## Why it will recur

Nothing about the click case was special. The preconditions are structural:
* uv's universal resolution locks every extra jointly, so ONE capping dependency (there, `inspect-ai`)
  holds the whole project on a vulnerable version;
* `pip-audit` is gating and correctly refuses to distinguish "reachable in this project" from
  "present in the environment" — `click.edit()` was never called anywhere in rebar;
* the retry logic in the job only retries DB-UNREACHABLE failures, so a real finding is not
  recheckable — which is the single most time-wasting property, because `recheck` is the first thing
  everyone tries.

## The knowledge that must not be rediscovered under time pressure

This is the substance of the ticket. It took several wrong turns to establish, including one
confidently-recorded wrong conclusion:
* `constraint-dependencies` can only NARROW an existing constraint set. Testing feasibility with it
  returns UNSATISFIABLE **as its expected output**, which reads as proof that the upgrade is
  impossible. It is not proof of anything. `override-dependencies` REPLACES the offending requirement
  and is the correct instrument.
* `uv lock --upgrade-package <pkg>` is a NO-OP against an upstream cap for the same reason.
* Overriding a cap is only safe when the cap is STALE rather than a real incompatibility, and that
  needs evidence (upstream issue/PR showing the incompatibility was fixed; the capped package
  importing and running under the newer version).
* An override must carry a REMOVE-WHEN condition, or it outlives its justification silently.
* `override-dependencies` is a workspace directive, NOT published in wheel metadata — so it changes
  this repo's lock only, and downstream consumers are unaffected.

## Out of scope

Changing the pip-audit job to be non-gating, or adding blanket suppressions. The gate did its job here
— it found a real advisory in the shipped environment. The problem is response latency, not the gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a short runbook exists (in `docs/`, discoverable from the pip-audit job's own failure output or
      a comment beside it) covering: how to tell a real finding from a DB-unreachable flake, that
      `recheck` cannot clear a real finding, the `override-dependencies` vs `constraint-dependencies`
      distinction, and the evidence required before overriding an upstream cap
- [ ] the runbook states the verification set for any lock intervention: `uv lock --check` under the
      uv versions in use, `uv sync --locked --extra dev`, and `pip-audit` over the whole resulting
      environment to confirm the old pin was masking nothing else
- [ ] a mechanism exists to notice an override whose REMOVE-WHEN condition has been met, rather than
      relying on someone happening to re-test — either a periodic check or a documented review trigger
- [ ] the runbook is linked from the pip-audit step so a person hitting the failure finds it without
      knowing it exists
- [ ] [operator-attested] the runbook is validated by walking the click/PYSEC-2026-2132 case through
      it and confirming it would have led to `override-dependencies` without the detour, with that
      walkthrough recorded on this ticket
data.title: Committed lock turns transitive-dep advisories into build stoppages
